html:
Brunei brought in a sharia criminal code in stages from 2014 to 2019, making it the first country in East Asia with sharia punishments at the national level.

The code, pushed by Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, set penalties such as amputation for theft and stoning for adultery and sex between men. Its final stage in 2019 caused boycotts of hotels owned by the sultan abroad, and he then extended a pause on the death penalty.

It grew from the idea of Brunei as a Malay Islamic Monarchy, built on the faith of its first sultan. Ordinary civil and commercial law still follows British models. See also Islam.
sum: Brunei brought in a sharia criminal code in stages from 2014 to 2019, making it the first country in East Asia with sharia punishments at the national level.
